Relational storage engines rely on Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) to guarantee durability by appending redo and undo records to sequential log files before dirty pages leave the in-memory buffer pool. Log-Structured Merge-tree (LSM-tree) storage engines buffer incoming write operations inside an ordered in-memory memtable backed by a sequential commit log. The Linux kernel virtual memory subsystem translates process address spaces through multi-level page tables and populates physical frames on demand via page fault handlers. In POSIX operating systems, the kernel delivers asynchronous notifications to processes using standardized software signals managed through per-process signal masks and handler tables. PostgreSQL declarative table partitioning divides a large logical table into smaller physical child partitions segmented by range, list, or hash boundaries. Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation represents IPv4 network prefixes by appending a bit-length suffix that defines the contiguous subnet mask boundary. HTTP/2 replaces plain-text request framing with a binary framing layer that multiplexes concurrent request and response streams over a single persistent TCP connection.
